Title: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
Research_Question: Can LLMs self-correct intrinsic reasoning errors via multi-turn verbal feedback without oracle hints?
Evaluation_Method: Multi-turn prompting (prompting model to find its own mistake)
Main_Contribution: Demonstrated that prompting-based intrinsic self-correction degrades accuracy without external feedback.
Similarity_to_StateShift: Both evaluate model performance after reasoning errors.
StateShift_Distinction: Huang et al. evaluate multi-turn prompting in frozen models. StateShift evaluates single-rollout continuous decoding across an RL post-training trajectory under counterfactual state matching.

Title: Training Language Models to Self-Correct via Reinforcement Learning (SCoRe)
Research_Question: Can multi-turn self-correction be learned through reinforcement learning?
Evaluation_Method: Two-turn RL objective rewarding Turn 2 improvements over Turn 1
Main_Contribution: Multi-turn RL framework explicitly trained to correct first-turn errors.
Similarity_to_StateShift: Both study RL and error correction in reasoning.
StateShift_Distinction: SCoRe explicitly trains and optimizes a multi-turn correction policy. StateShift evaluates standard single-turn RLVR (GRPO) trained ONLY on final answer rewards, uncovering an emergent state-transition recovery effect.

Title: GPT-4 Doesn't Know When It's Wrong in Self-Correction
Research_Question: Do frontier models possess calibrated self-verification capabilities during self-correction?
Evaluation_Method: Multi-turn prompting and prompt-based self-verification tests
Main_Contribution: Showed prompt-based self-correction frequently hallucinates errors or confirms invalid steps.
StateShift_Distinction: Evaluates unprompted single-rollout recovery using deterministic ground-truth verifiers rather than prompt-based self-verification.

Title: DeepScaleR: Surpassing O1-Preview with a 1.5B Model by Scaling RL
Research_Question: How does scaling RL post-training compute enhance mathematical reasoning?
Main_Contribution: Demonstrated that scaling GRPO post-training on math unit tests produces massive Pass@1 gains.
Similarity_to_StateShift: StateShift evaluates the open-source DeepScaleR checkpoint lineage.
StateShift_Distinction: DeepScaleR reports only aggregate Pass@1 accuracy. StateShift discovers that DeepScaleR's gains are state-selective (+11.76 pp recovery interaction), revealing non-monotonic recovery dynamics.

Title: Let's Verify Step by Step
Research_Question: Does process-level supervision (PRM) outperform outcome-level supervision (ORM)?
Evaluation_Method: Human-labeled step-level verification (PRM800K) and Best-of-N search
Main_Contribution: Established that process supervision with trained neural reward models guides beam search.
Similarity_to_StateShift: Both focus on intermediate reasoning steps.
StateShift_Distinction: Lightman et al. train neural process reward models for search guidance. StateShift uses deterministic execution verifiers to measure intrinsic policy recovery under perturbed states.

Title: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models
Research_Question: Can Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) scale mathematical reasoning without a critic model?
Evaluation_Method: Rule-based outcome evaluation on GSM8K and MATH
Main_Contribution: Introduced GRPO and showed RLVR surpasses pure SFT.
Similarity_to_StateShift: Algorithmic foundation of the evaluated models.
StateShift_Distinction: DeepSeekMath measures only aggregate correctness. StateShift formalizes the state-conditioned evaluation framework.
